proves.claim: a historical version-three receipt retains same-row array merging while version four reports the exact plan shard conflict.

merge.io-mechanical-replay.version-three.why: Recorded receipts must replay under the policy version that produced them, while current policy refuses divergent edits to one row.

proves.claim: the mechanical merge index preserves independent plan shard row additions from both branches.

merge.io-plan-shard-conflicts.disjoint-a.why: Concurrent shard additions must compose without discarding either contributor's row.

proves.claim: different edits to the same existing plan shard row remain a conflict.

merge.io-plan-shard-conflicts.divergent-.why: Mechanical resolution must not choose one side of a genuine same-row edit.

proves.claim: different definitions of the same newly added plan shard row remain a conflict.

merge.io-plan-shard-conflicts.divergent-.why: Two branches that introduce the same row differently must not create an ambiguous shard.

proves.claim: deleting a shard while the other branch edits it remains a conflict in both orders.

merge.io-plan-shard-conflicts.deletion-v.why: Deletion must not silently erase or resurrect content changed by the other branch.

proves.claim: the plan index merges by cell row, a same-row edit refuses, and the test tiers file still merges by row.

merge.logic-manifest.plan-index-by-row.why: Many parallel children edit the plan index; a plain text merge conflicts although they touch different rows.

proves.claim: two branches that each add a plan shard row and a data-read row compose with both rows in both orders.

merge.plan-data.composes-both-rows.why: A plain text merge of two appended rows conflicted although neither side changed the other's row.

proves.claim: a data-read row and a shard row edited differently on both sides still refuse MERGE_CONFLICT.

merge.plan-data.refuses-divergent-rows.why: Composing must never silently pick one side of a real edit conflict.

proves.claim: a conflict in any other file still refuses.

merge.plan-data.refuses-other-conflicts.why: Composition applies only to the plan and data-read files.

proves.claim: an item whose own branch merges cleanly gets no conflict warning although its seat checkout branch conflicts.

merge.carriage.clean-branch-no-warning.why: A warning judged from the seat's checkout branch told builders to fix conflicts they did not have (#3820).

proves.claim: an item whose own branch really conflicts with the new main gets one warning naming the conflicting file.

merge.carriage.real-conflict-one-warning.why: A real conflict must be named once, with its file, so the builder acts on it (#3820).

proves.claim: every merge-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

merge.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: every merge test that reads repo files names the exact files it reads in its header, never a whole cell.

merge.inputs.declared.why: Affected-test selection can only see a reader whose inputs are declared.

proves.claim: the reader rule reports no undeclared reader in the merge tests with the outside-src rule on.

merge.inputs.rule-clean.why: The rule going on must not turn this cell red.

proves.claim: a source composition whose controller started and then threw rejects with the retained path in its message and the thrown error as cause, and keeps the folder.

merge.compose.custody-unknown-keeps-caus.why: The finally block hid the real error behind the custody refusal, so a gate throw and an unverified cleanup looked the same (about 900 board facts).

proves.claim: a composition that confirmed terminal custody, or never started, removes its folder.

merge.compose.custody-terminal-removes.why: Keeping the cause must not change when folders are retained or removed.
